United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO)

description.narrative: The UNESCO Creative Cities Network (UCCN) is an expanding international city network, with a growing potential to innovate on culture driven urban development. Its member cities have developed and experimented innovative ways to integrate culture and creativity at the core of their policies, strategies and plans, which significantly contributes to sustainable development. As a UNESCO flagship city programme, the Network has contributed to strengthening advocacy efforts towards the integration of culture in the international sustainable development agenda. With its 350 member cities in more than 100 countries, the Network has a growing voice in international discussions on cities and sustainable urban development. As a result, the number of cities applying to each Call for Application has also been rising. The Network covers a variety of cities, from small-sized settlements to metropolises, within various economic, social, political and environmental settings. This urban diversity allows the emergence of a wide range of policies, strategies and practices at the city level aimed at dealing with common challenges of our time. Over the last years, the Network has significantly reshaped its management mechanisms. UNESCO’s leading role as the Secretariat of the Network has been consolidated, covering different action areas notably the designation process, the membership monitoring excercise, the organization of the annual conferences, knowledge development, awareness raising and communication activities, among many others. Committed to fostering sustainable urban development through creativity and culture, the Network supports the localization of the 2030 Agenda, more specifically Goal 11 – Sustainable Cities and Communities, and the 2022 MONDIACULT Declaration, identifying culture as a “global public good”, with a view to integrating it as a standalone goal in the post-2030 international development agenda. The UCCN Secretariat also coordinates the UNESCO Cities Platform, which was established in 2019 encompassing 8 networks and programmes on or closely related to cities across all 5 programme sectors. Aimed at strengthening the Organization’s crosscutting approach on sustainable urban development, the Platform and its members are privileged partners of the UCCN to extend its impact and outreach, combining culture with education, sciences, information and communication in devising comprehensive and effective solutions to development issues.
